# perft_suite_960_mid.txt - Chess960 MIDGAME positions where castling is legal.
#
#   ./perft --make all -d 4 -f perft_suite_960_mid.txt
#   ./perft --check --nobulk --make all -d 3 -f perft_suite_960_mid.txt
#
# perft_suite_960.txt holds the 960 START positions, and they are nearly useless for castling:
# it is not even reachable in the four plies that suite runs. These are positions where the back
# rank has opened up, king and rooks are still home, and castling is legal RIGHT NOW - including
# the cases where the rook's castling destination is its own square.
#
# Generated by walking random legal moves with STOCKFISH (not libchess, so the positions do not
# depend on the generator under test), keeping only positions where some legal move is the king
# moving onto one of its own rooks. Counts from Stockfish under UCI_Chess960.
#
# Two batches from different seeds, 900 positions. The first found both defects below; the
# second was generated afterwards, independently, and passed clean - which is the evidence that
# the fixes are complete rather than merely fitted to the cases that exposed them.
#
# Defect 1 (move generation): castling legality tested the king's path against attacks computed
# with the castling ROOK STILL IN PLACE. In Chess960 the rook can have an enemy slider behind it
# on the back rank - white king d1, white rook b1, BLACK QUEEN a1 - so castling queenside vacates
# b1 and the queen then attacks c1. libchess generated d1b1; Stockfish did not. Standard chess
# cannot produce this, because the queenside rook starts on a1 with nothing behind it.
#
# Defect 2 (make/unmake): undo_move() restored the castling rook to its source before clearing
# its destination, and in Chess960 those can be the same square. See perft_suite_960.txt.
